fields.description:
## Context / Problem
rebar's own LLM HTTP clients ignore the standard proxy environment (`HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY`). On a host whose network egress goes only through a proxy, every gate LLM call fails before it leaves the host, and `review-plan` and completion-verifier closes return INDETERMINATE.

Observed 2026-11-22 PST in the Claude Code Bash sandbox. Its egress is a proxy at `localhost:<port>`, named in `HTTPS_PROXY`, and it has no direct DNS (`socket.getaddrinfo('api.anthropic.com', 443)` raises `gaierror 8`). `review-plan` there returned INDETERMINATE three times, once for each of sporting-feudalist-bluet and charitable-tyrannical-hydra plus a retry. Every LLM call logged `All models from FallbackModel failed (2 sub-exceptions)`, and the failure classifier labelled it "Transient connection blip". The same reviews passed outside the sandbox. In the same sandbox, `curl` and the venv's plain `anthropic` SDK both reached `https://api.anthropic.com`, because both use `HTTPS_PROXY`.

## Root cause (reproduced)
- The sub-exceptions, printed by wrapping `run_failure.logger` around a `get_runner(resolve_gate_config('.')).run(RunRequest(..., execution_mode="single_turn"))` call: both FallbackModel candidates raise `ModelAPIError('Connection error.') <- APIConnectionError <- httpx.ConnectError <- gaierror(8, 'nodename nor servname provided, or not known')`. The client resolved the host itself, so it never used the proxy.
- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py::_build_retrying_anthropic_provider` builds `http_module.AsyncClient(transport=<AsyncTenacityTransport wrapping http_module.AsyncHTTPTransport()>)` (around line 280-293), and the httpx2 variant builds the same thing (lines 125, 132). httpx 0.28.1 sets `allow_env_proxies = trust_env and transport is None`, so passing any explicit transport turns the environment proxy off.
- In the observed failure the gate targeted `https://api.anthropic.com` directly: it does not use a loopback `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, by design (`_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`, bug sue-skimp-tear). That is the default, not the only case: a candidate's own `endpoint`, a non-loopback `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateway, `REBAR_LLM_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROXY`, and local OpenAI-compatible servers all reach other hosts, often on loopback.
- Controlled experiment: `_build_retrying_anthropic_provider(base_url="https://api.anthropic.com", cfg=LLMConfig())` with the default wrapped transport fails with `ConnectError gaierror 8`. The same call with `_wrapped_transport=httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(proxy=<HTTPS_PROXY>)` returns a completion. One variable changed.
- Same class, not yet exercised: the OpenAI-compatible client in `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` (around line 306-307) passes `transport=httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport()` explicitly. Bedrock goes through boto3, which reads the proxy environment.

## Approach
Make rebar's LLM transports honour the standard proxy environment variables (`HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY`) with standard-library semantics. This is httpx's own default behaviour, with 3 deliberate differences listed below. Every explicit `AsyncHTTPTransport` that rebar creates for an LLM client becomes a transport that picks, per request URL, the scheme's proxy, else `ALL_PROXY`, or a direct connection. The retry wrapper and timeouts stay as they are, and the retry wrapper sits above the routing so proxied and direct requests retry alike. No new config key, env var or flag: the change only respects ambient proxy variables that httpx already applies by default.

### Implementation
- `_env_proxy_aware_transport(http_module)` in `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`, next to `_build_httpx2_tenacity_transport`, reads the variables once at construction with `urllib.request.getproxies_environment()`.
  - No `http`/`https`/`all` proxy set: it returns `http_module.AsyncHTTPTransport()`, the exact object built before, so behaviour is unchanged.
  - A proxy set: it returns `_EnvProxyRoutingTransport`, which holds one direct `http_module.AsyncHTTPTransport()` and one `http_module.AsyncHTTPTransport(proxy=<url>)` per distinct proxy URL, built up front. It implements the async transport protocol (`handle_async_request`, `__aenter__`, `__aexit__`, `aclose`) itself rather than subclassing, so one class serves httpx and httpx2 and the module imports neither at load time. A proxy value without a scheme gets `http://`, as in httpx.
  - Per request: a loopback host goes direct; a host matched by `NO_PROXY` (`urllib.request.proxy_bypass`, whose environment matcher applies whenever proxy variables are set) goes direct; otherwise the scheme's proxy, else `ALL_PROXY`.
- Deliberate differences from httpx's default client:
  1. Only the environment is read. The macOS/Windows system-proxy fallback in `getproxies()` is not consulted, so a host with no proxy variable keeps its current direct behaviour.
  2. Loopback hosts (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0`, `*.localhost`; rebar's existing `_LOOPBACK_HOSTS` set) always connect directly, whether or not `NO_PROXY` lists them. A proxy cannot reach this machine's loopback, and local LLM endpoints (a candidate `endpoint`, a local OpenAI-compatible server, a loopback base URL allowed by `REBAR_LLM_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROXY`) connect directly today.
  3. A proxy value no transport can use (unknown scheme such as `ftp://`, SOCKS without `socksio`) is skipped with a WARNING that names the variable but never its value (it may carry credentials). The request falls back to the next applicable proxy or goes direct, as it did before, instead of every LLM call failing at construction.
- Transports are constructed through `http_module.AsyncHTTPTransport` looked up at call time, so the existing `monkeypatch.setattr(httpx, "AsyncHTTPTransport", ...)` test seam keeps working.
- `_build_retrying_anthropic_provider`: the default wrapped transport becomes `_env_proxy_aware_transport(http_module)` for both the httpx path (`AsyncTenacityTransport`) and the httpx2 path (`_build_httpx2_tenacity_transport`, whose own fallback defaults use it too). An explicit `_wrapped_transport` is still used verbatim. The retry config, `_validate_response`, timeouts and the `max_retries=0` guard are untouched.
- `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` OpenAI-compatible client: `transport=_env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx)` instead of `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport()`; timeout unchanged.
- Failure disposition is unchanged: a connection failure to the proxy is an `httpx.NetworkError` and retries like any connection failure; a proxy refusal (`httpx.ProxyError`) is not retried, as today for non-network transport errors.

### Survey of other explicit transports in `src/rebar`
No other client turns off the proxy environment. The MCP introspection client (`_mcp_auth.py`) passes `transport=None` by default, so httpx applies the environment. Jira Data Center uses `requests`. The review-bot Gerrit client and the terraform grounding probe use `urllib.request` openers, which include the environment `ProxyHandler`. Bedrock uses boto3. Nothing to file.

### Tests (new `tests/unit/test_llm_env_proxy.py`, offline)
A recording factory replaces `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport` (the existing seam) and records the `proxy=` each transport was built with; requests are served by `httpx.MockTransport`. An explicit `clean_proxy_env` fixture removes every `*_proxy` variable first, so the tests are hermetic on proxied hosts.
- Anthropic provider, `HTTPS_PROXY` set: a request to `https://api.anthropic.com` is handled by the transport built with that proxy (failed on main).
- `NO_PROXY` matching the host: direct, while an unmatched host in the same client still uses the proxy.
- No proxy variables: exactly one transport is built, with no `proxy=`, and it handles the request.
- `ALL_PROXY` is used when the scheme-specific variable is absent.
- An unusable `ALL_PROXY` is skipped with a credential-free warning, and does not disable a usable `HTTPS_PROXY`.
- Loopback endpoints (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `*.localhost`) connect directly with a proxy set and no `NO_PROXY`.
- An explicit `_wrapped_transport` bypasses proxy selection.
- The httpx2 retry wrapper routes through the proxy and honours `NO_PROXY` (skipped when `httpx2` is not installed; it is installed in the dev environment).
- The OpenAI-compatible client built by `ProviderSession` uses `HTTP_PROXY` for an `http://` endpoint, goes direct for a `NO_PROXY` host and for a local server without `NO_PROXY`, and is unchanged with no proxy variables.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A unit test builds the Anthropic provider client with a proxy set in the environment and asserts that the request is routed through that proxy; it fails on main before the fix.
- [ ] A unit test asserts a host matched by `NO_PROXY` connects directly, and that with no proxy variables set, behaviour is unchanged (direct connection).
- [ ] The OpenAI-compatible client in `providers.py` gets the same treatment, with a test.
- [ ] `make verify` passes on the change.
- [ ] `rebar review-plan` on a ticket, run inside the Claude Code Bash sandbox with `api.anthropic.com` allowed, returns a real verdict (not INDETERMINATE from connection errors). The run log is recorded in a comment.
